notes: C runtime functions under the Windows x64 convention (args RCX, RDX, R8, R9; result RAX). Register offsets are Ghidra x86-64: RAX 0, RCX 8, RDX 16, RBX 24, RSP 32, RBP 40, RSI 48, RDI 56, R8 128, R9 136, R12-R15 160-184. Preserved: the non-volatile integer registers; XMM and flags are left unknown (sound, less precise). Every entry is a declared assumption.

entries.name: memcpy
entries.notes: dst[0, n) = src[0, n); returns dst. Exact only when n is proven constant at the call.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (MS docs: memcpy, memmove); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: memset
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (MS docs: memset); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: strcpy
entries.notes: For a defined call (src NUL-terminated, dst writable and large enough, no overlap -- otherwise undefined behaviour): dst[0] = src[0] when it returns (strcpy copies at least the terminating NUL, src[0] first); the rest has an extent known only at run time: all other memory is unknown. Returns dst.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (MS docs: strcpy -- the non-_s form has no invalid-parameter handler call); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: strcat
entries.notes: Writes an extent known only at run time (strncpy with n == 0 writes nothing; strcat writes after dst's string): no memory is kept. Returns dst.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (MS docs: strcat); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: abort
entries.notes: Never returns to its caller (C11 7.22.4.1): the paths through it end there. Uses no pointer it receives (observes nothing).
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.22.4.1 (raises SIGABRT); MS docs: abort (signal handler, _set_abort_behavior); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: longjmp
entries.notes: Never returns to its caller (C11 7.13.2.1, _Noreturn): only the paths after the call end; the setjmp side is not modeled here (an opaque call). Reads the jmp_buf rcx points to (observes rcx).

registered: unwind handlers of the frames left (__finally blocks, C++ destructors under MSVC x64 unwinding semantics)

entries.callbacks_evidence: MS docs: longjmp (x64: uses exception-handling unwinding semantics); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: strlen
entries.notes: Reads memory of unknown extent: the result is left unknown; memory unchanged.
entries.callbacks_evidence: ISO C17 7.24 string / memory functions: no user code, no allocation (MS docs: strlen); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: malloc
entries.notes: Returns a new block's address (no program data flows into it; fresh: never an address of memory existing before the call, the stack included) of rcx bytes, or null (docs 25.79: the size is used only where a null test dominates the access). Heap bookkeeping is not program-visible memory (assumption).

registered: new handler (_set_new_handler; malloc/realloc call it on failure when _set_new_mode(1))

entries.callbacks_evidence: MS docs: malloc, _set_new_mode, _set_new_handler; MS docs: _CrtSetAllocHook (debug CRT: every allocation call); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: calloc
entries.notes: Returns a new block's address (no program data flows into it; fresh: never an address of memory existing before the call, the stack included) of rcx * rdx bytes (zero-filled), or null; the product is taken only when it does not overflow (docs 25.79: the size is used only where a null test dominates the access). Heap bookkeeping is not program-visible memory (assumption).

registered: new handler (_set_new_handler; malloc/realloc call it on failure when _set_new_mode(1))

entries.callbacks_evidence: MS docs: calloc, malloc, _set_new_mode, _set_new_handler; MS docs: _CrtSetAllocHook (debug CRT: every allocation call); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: free
entries.notes: Assumes no use after free: the freed block's contents are not read again. Uses no pointer it receives on program-visible memory and keeps none (observes nothing).
entries.callbacks_evidence: MS docs: free (frees its argument's block); _CrtSetAllocHook (debug CRT: the hook runs on every free); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)

entries.name: realloc
entries.notes: Returns a block holding the old contents: the same object as the old pointer, assuming the old pointer is not used afterwards (no-use-of-old-pointer-after-realloc); realloc(NULL, n) is a fresh block.

registered: new handler (_set_new_handler; malloc/realloc call it on failure when _set_new_mode(1))

entries.callbacks_evidence: MS docs: realloc, _set_new_mode (may free / move the old block); MS docs: _CrtSetAllocHook (debug CRT: every allocation call); audited 2026-10-21 (TDO_v2 forward step 0, docs 25.33)
